pois.name: Teide
pois.description: Spain's highest volcano at 3,715 metres. A UNESCO World Heritage National Park. Its lunar lava landscapes and cable car to the summit make it the most visited place in Spain.
pois.shortDescription: Spain's highest volcano, UNESCO World Heritage Site

pois.name: Santa Cruz de Tenerife
pois.description: Capital of Tenerife and home to Spain's most famous Carnival, declared an International Tourist Interest event. Major commercial port, García Sanabria Park and the modern architecture of Calatrava's Auditorium.
pois.shortDescription: Capital of Tenerife, home to Spain's most famous Carnival

pois.name: Los Gigantes
pois.description: Cliffs up to 600 metres tall dropping vertically into the Atlantic. Boat trips to spot dolphins and pilot whales in their natural habitat. The most dramatic village on the west coast of Tenerife.
pois.shortDescription: 600m cliffs and whale watching on the west coast

pois.name: Playa de Las Teresitas
pois.shortDescription: Saharan golden sand and calm sheltered waters just 10 minutes from Santa Cruz
pois.description:
The most famous beach in northern Tenerife has an origin as remarkable as its appearance: its **golden sand was shipped directly from the Sahara** in the 1970s, transforming what was once a pebble cove into one of the most beautiful beaches in the Canary Islands. Just ten minutes from Santa Cruz, it is the coastal escape of the capital.

### The visit
A nearly one-kilometre breakwater shields the bay from Atlantic swells, creating permanently calm water ideal for family swimming. Imperial palms line the promenade and the fishing village of San Andrés — with its legendary fresh fish restaurants — is a short stroll away. Just metres from the beach, the **Castillo de San Andrés**, a 16th-century fortress, adds a historical dimension to the setting.

### Before you go
- 🌅 In summer, arrive before 11am — the beach fills fast, especially at weekends
- 🚌 Bus 910 from Santa Cruz bus station — 20 minutes, €1.35
- 🐟 Don't leave without eating in San Andrés: red prawns and grilled limpets are unmissable
- 🏊 Calm water year-round thanks to the breakwater — perfect even for very young children
- 🅿️ Free parking next to the beach, but fills up early in summer

### Recommendation
Combine a swim with lunch at a San Andrés restaurant and a visit to the castle: Las Teresitas is more than a beach — it is a complete northern Tenerife experience.

pois.name: Playa de Los Cristianos
pois.shortDescription: The beating heart of the south: dark sand beach with Tenerife's liveliest harbour
pois.description:
The tourist heart of southern Tenerife beats strongest in Los Cristianos. Its **dark volcanic sand** beach and warm sheltered waters share the spotlight with one of the busiest ports in the Canary Islands — the daily departure point for ferries to La Gomera, catamaran trips and the island's best cetacean watching tours.

### The visit
Los Cristianos retains the soul of a fishing village absorbed by modern tourism, and that is much of its charm. The seafront promenade blends beach bars and terraces with local shops, the municipal market offers genuine Canarian cooking and the atmosphere at sunset in the square is pure southern Tenerife. For water lovers, pilot whale watching tours — the whales are resident in these waters year-round — deliver one of the most memorable wildlife encounters in the Atlantic.

### Before you go
- 🐬 Book whale watching for early morning — sea conditions are calmer and sightings more frequent
- ⛵ To visit La Gomera, ferries depart from here several times a day (45 minutes)
- 🍽️ The municipal market and the streets of the old village are the best area for Canarian cooking
- 🚌 Bus 111 from Las Américas and bus 111/487 from Costa Adeje — very frequent service
- 🏖️ The beach is quieter at the southern end, near the harbour

### Recommendation
Start the day with a swim, have papas arrugadas with mojo at the market, and board a boat in the afternoon: Los Cristianos is made to be enjoyed at several different paces.

pois.name: Playa del Duque
pois.shortDescription: The south's most exclusive beach: white sand, turquoise water and luxury hotels
pois.description:
If there is one beach in Tenerife that could be mistaken for the Caribbean, it is Playa del Duque. **Fine pale golden sand, clear turquoise water** and the backdrop of the south's most exclusive hotels create an elegance that is rare on Spanish coastlines.

### The visit
The water is shallow and calm — ideal for children and for anyone who prefers their swimming without drama. At the northern end of the beach, where rocks emerge from the water, there is an excellent snorkelling spot with rock fish, sea urchins and crabs. Ten minutes' walk away is **Puerto Colón**, Costa Adeje's major marina, from which catamarans sail to Los Gigantes and whale watching tours with guaranteed sightings depart daily. The whole Duque waterfront, with its palm-lined promenade and hotel terraces, is designed to be enjoyed at leisure.

### Before you go
- 🅿️ The free car park next to the beach has limited spaces — arrive before 10am in peak season
- 🤿 Bring a snorkel mask: the northern rocky end has genuinely interesting marine life
- 🚤 Catamaran and cetacean tours depart from Puerto Colón (10 min walk) — book online in advance
- 🍹 The Duque promenade has beach bars and terraces for lunch without leaving the sand
- 🚌 Bus 473 from Los Cristianos and Santa Cruz

### Recommendation
Morning on the beach, afternoon on a catamaran to Los Gigantes, dinner on a Costa Adeje terrace: Playa del Duque is the perfect base for a luxurious day in the south of Tenerife.

pois.name: Playa de La Arena
pois.shortDescription: Black volcanic sand, Blue Flag quality and direct views of La Gomera
pois.description:
One of the best beaches on Tenerife's west coast, and one of the least known to international visitors. **Perfectly rounded black volcanic sand**, surprisingly clear water and direct views of La Gomera's silhouette on the horizon: La Arena is exactly the kind of beach that makes you feel you have discovered something all your own.

### The visit
The cove is sheltered from the wind by the surrounding hillsides, keeping the water calm and the air temperature several degrees warmer than the south coast. It holds a **Blue Flag** award consistently thanks to water quality and beach facilities. The seafront promenade of Puerto de Santiago wraps around the beach and concentrates some of the west coast's best fresh fish restaurants. Five minutes by car are the Los Gigantes cliffs, departure point for the island's best whale and dolphin watching tours.

### Before you go
- 🤿 The southern end of the beach — where rocks meet sand — is an excellent snorkelling spot with abundant marine life
- 🐋 Combine the visit with a whale watching tour from Los Gigantes harbour, 5 minutes by car
- 🏖️ Black sand retains heat: one of the warmest beaches on the island even in winter
- 🐟 Try the fresh fish at the restaurants along Puerto de Santiago's seafront promenade
- 🅿️ Park in the village streets (free) or the small car park next to the promenade

### Recommendation
La Arena works perfectly as a base for the west coast: swim, snorkel, lunch in the village and in the afternoon board a boat to watch whales at Los Gigantes.

pois.name: Playa de Benijo
pois.shortDescription: Wild beach in the heart of Anaga: black rocks, Atlantic swells and no crowds
pois.description:
There are beautiful beaches in Tenerife, and then there is Benijo. Tucked into the far north-eastern tip of the island, inside the **Anaga Rural Park**, it is Tenerife's wildest and most authentic beach: no sun loungers, no beach bars, no hotels in sight. Just the open Atlantic, black volcanic sand and the **Roques de Anaga** rising from the water in front of the shore.

### The visit
The Roques — two volcanic formations that stand like sentinels over the bay — are the photographic icon of Benijo and one of the most recognisable landscapes in the entire archipelago. The drive to reach the beach is part of the experience: mountain hairpins through laurel forests, terraced farms and tiny Anaga hamlets that seem to have stopped in time. The surf is open Atlantic and can be powerful, particularly in winter.

### Before you go
- ⚠️ Swells can be dangerous — check sea conditions before swimming and never enter with a red flag flying
- 📸 Golden hour at sunrise and sunset is the best time to photograph the Roques
- 🚗 TF-134 road from La Laguna towards Taganana — narrow mountain curves, drive with care
- 🅿️ The small car park next to the beach is free — on weekends it fills early
- 🎒 No facilities of any kind on the beach — bring water, food and take all your rubbish home

### Recommendation
Go at first light, when the sun strikes the Roques and the beach is almost empty: Benijo at that moment is one of the most special places in the entire Canary Islands.

pois.name: El Médano
pois.shortDescription: Spain's windsurfing and kitesurfing capital: constant trade winds, long sandy beach and a young crowd
pois.description:
El Médano is Tenerife's different beach. While the rest of the south chases windless sunshine, this village has embraced the **constant Atlantic trade winds** and made them its greatest asset: it is the best windsurfing and kitesurfing spot in Spain, and a global reference for light-wind water sports. Young, cosmopolitan, and always in motion.

### The visit
More than **two kilometres of fine sand** flanked by the wind, with the unmistakable **Roque del Moro** — a volcanic rock tooth rising from the sea — presiding over the bay. Windsurfing and kitesurfing schools operate directly on the beach, equipment hire is very affordable and the international instructors make El Médano the best place in Spain to learn these sports. If you prefer swimming without a board, **Playa Grande**, to the south, offers calmer water. And afterwards, the central square with its cafés and terraces is one of the liveliest in the south.

### Before you go
- 🏄 Wind is strongest in the afternoon — if you want to learn, mornings are gentler
- 🌊 Playa Grande, south of the Roque del Moro, has calmer water for non-wind-sport swimmers
- 🚗 Reina Sofía Airport (TFS) is just 5 minutes away — ideal as a first or last stop on your trip
- 🚌 Bus 116 from Los Cristianos (30 min)
- 🍺 The central square and surrounding terraces are the hub of the evening atmosphere — unmissable at sunset

### Recommendation
Arrive in the afternoon, find a table on the central square terrace and watch the kitesurfers cross the bay with the Roque del Moro behind them: one of the best scenes the south of Tenerife has to offer.

pois.name: Car rental in Tenerife
pois.shortDescription: Essential for exploring the island: how, where and how much to rent a car
pois.description:
Tenerife is a large and varied island, and **renting a car is the freest and most efficient way to explore it**. From Reina Sofía Airport (south) or Los Rodeos Airport (north), you have immediate access to all major rental companies. Prices are among the most competitive in Europe thanks to strong competition and the Canary Islands' special tax regime.

### The visit
With a car, in a single day you can combine Teide in the morning, the Los Gigantes cliffs at midday and a sunset at El Médano. Without a car, that same route would take two or three days by public transport. The TF-1 motorway links the south with the north in under 45 minutes, and the TF-5 connects Santa Cruz to Puerto de la Cruz in 30 minutes. Mountain roads (Masca, Anaga) require care but are perfectly manageable in a standard car.

### Before you go
- 🛬 Always book from home via DiscoverCars or similar — up to 40% cheaper than airport desk prices
- 📋 You need a driving licence, credit card and to be over 21 (some operators require 25)
- ⛽ Petrol stations are plentiful in the south — in the north and mountains, fill up before heading up
- 🔑 Automatic cars sell out fast in peak season: book in advance
- 🅿️ Parking in Santa Cruz and Puerto de la Cruz can be tricky — use paid car parks

### Recommendation
Book online at least 48h before arrival, choose full cover with no excess, and plan routes anticlockwise to make the most of daylight.

pois.name: TITSA — Tenerife Buses
pois.shortDescription: The inter-urban bus network connecting the whole island affordably
pois.description:
**TITSA** (Transportes Interurbanos de Tenerife S.A.) is the public bus network connecting virtually every corner of the island, from Santa Cruz to El Médano, from Puerto de la Cruz to Los Gigantes. It is the most affordable way to get around and an authentic local experience.

### The visit
The most useful lines for visitors are **111** (Santa Cruz – Los Cristianos, express), **343** (Santa Cruz – La Laguna – Puerto de la Cruz), **348** (Puerto de la Cruz – Teide – Los Cristianos, the island's great panoramic route) and **910** (Santa Cruz – Las Teresitas). Buses are modern with air conditioning and WiFi on main routes. The **BONO card** gives 50% discounts compared to cash fares.

### Before you go
- 📱 Download the TITSA app or check titsa.com for up-to-date timetables — Sunday service is reduced
- 💳 Load the BONO card at main stations — it pays off from your second trip
- 🕐 Express lines to the south (111, 110) are the fastest and most frequent
- 🏔️ Line 348 crosses Teide National Park — a scenic route that requires no car
- 🎫 A single cash ticket from Santa Cruz to the south costs ~€3.50; with BONO, under €2

### Recommendation
If you are only visiting the south or north, the bus is enough. If you want to explore Teide, Anaga or Masca, rent a car for at least those days.

pois.name: La Laguna — Historic Quarter
pois.shortDescription: UNESCO World Heritage city with the most beautiful colonial architecture in the Canary Islands
pois.description:
San Cristóbal de La Laguna was the first unwalled city in Spanish history — a 15th-century urban experiment that directly influenced the design of cities such as Lima, Havana and San Juan de Puerto Rico. UNESCO recognised it as a World Heritage Site in 1999. Its historic quarter, with black lava streets and colourful colonial façades, is the most beautiful in the Canary Islands.

### The visit
The main axis is **Calle Obispo Rey Redondo**, flanked by noble mansions, baroque churches and the Convent of Santa Clara. **La Laguna Cathedral**, built in the 20th century in an austere neo-Gothic style, houses the Cristo de La Laguna, Tenerife's most venerated image. **Plaza del Adelantado**, the heart of the city, is home to the municipal market, the Town Hall and some of the island's best cafés. The city is also home to the oldest university in the Canary Islands, giving it a permanently young and bohemian atmosphere.

### Before you go
- 🚋 The tram connects La Laguna to Santa Cruz in 30 minutes — the most comfortable way to get there
- 🕐 Allow at least 3 hours for the historic quarter; there is a great deal to see and explore
- ☕ The side streets off Calle Herradores and around it are where the best local cafés and restaurants are
- 📸 Morning light on the colonial façades is the best for photography
- 🎭 During Holy Week, La Laguna hosts one of the most impressive processions in Spain

### Recommendation
Combine La Laguna with the Anaga Rural Park: leave the city heading northeast and within 20 minutes you will be in a cinematic laurel forest.

pois.name: Puerto de la Cruz
pois.shortDescription: The north's tourist capital: gardens, natural pools and Tenerife's original resort town
pois.description:
Puerto de la Cruz was Tenerife's first modern tourist destination, chosen in the 20th century by European — and especially British — aristocracy seeking an escape from cold winters. Today it retains that cosmopolitan charm of a town that has been welcoming the world for decades without losing its Canarian identity.

### The visit
The heart of the town is **Plaza del Charco**, surrounded by century-old dragon trees and palms, with terraces that invite you to linger. The **Lago Martiánez pools**, designed by local artist César Manrique, are a marvel of organic Canarian architecture: saltwater pools of different sizes integrated into the black volcanic landscape, with the Atlantic as a backdrop. The **Botanical Garden** — one of Spain's oldest — houses tropical species brought from around the world. And just 10 minutes away is **Loro Parque**, the world's most award-winning zoo.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Lago Martiánez has an entrance fee (~€8) but is worth every cent — arrive in the morning
- 🚌 Bus 343 from Santa Cruz (45 min) and Bus 101/102 from Los Gigantes
- 🛍️ The Tuesday and Saturday market is the best for local produce
- 🌴 The Botanical Garden is 10 minutes' walk from the centre — impossible to miss
- 🍷 Calle Blanco and its surroundings have the best bars and restaurants

### Recommendation
Arrive in the morning, spend the first hours at the Martiánez pools, have lunch in the centre and head to Loro Parque in the afternoon: Puerto de la Cruz is a place to be enjoyed without rushing.

pois.name: Loro Parque
pois.shortDescription: The world's most awarded zoo: orcas, whales, penguins and the largest parrot collection
pois.description:
Founded in 1972 as a parrot park, Loro Parque has evolved into one of the most highly rated zoological parks on the planet, repeatedly awarded best zoo in the world by TripAdvisor. Its state-of-the-art facilities, species conservation programmes and orca and dolphin shows make it Tenerife's biggest family attraction.

### The visit
The park houses more than 30 primate species, the only **orcas in Europe** outside SeaWorld, one of the largest captive **Antarctic penguin** colonies in the world, sharks, crocodiles and the world's largest parrot collection with more than 3,000 specimens of 350 species. Orca, dolphin and sea lion shows take place several times a day. PlanetPenguin, the penguin habitat, simulates Antarctica with real snow.

### Before you go
- 🎟️ Buy tickets online — up to 15% cheaper and no queues
- 🕘 Arrive at opening (10am) to catch the first shows without crowds
- 🐋 The orca show has limited capacity — arrive 20 minutes early to get a seat
- 🚌 Bus 343/107 from Puerto de la Cruz towards Loro Parque (dedicated stop)
- ☀️ The park requires a full day to see everything — bring sunscreen and water

### Recommendation
Arrive at 10am, attend the orca show first (10:30am), then explore PlanetPenguin and the aquariums, and end the day with the dolphins: Loro Parque is designed for a full day without getting bored.

pois.name: Pyramids of Güímar
pois.shortDescription: Mysterious stepped structures that Thor Heyerdahl linked to ancient Egypt
pois.description:
In the coastal town of Güímar, on the southeast coast of Tenerife, stand six **stepped pyramids of black volcanic stone** whose origin remains debated. Norwegian explorer Thor Heyerdahl — famous for the Kon-Tiki expedition — studied them in the 1990s and proposed that they were not simply agricultural stone piles but intentional constructions with astronomical alignment, possibly linked to pre-Columbian trade routes.

### The visit
The ethnographic park created by Heyerdahl includes the pyramids, a museum with reproductions of reed boats and navigation objects, and gardens of endemic plants. The pyramids' alignment with the summer solstice is the strongest argument for intentional construction. The background landscape, with Teide dominating the horizon, adds an almost mystical dimension to the site.

### Before you go
- 🎟️ Entrance ~€12; guided tours available in several languages
- 🕐 Allow 2–3 hours — the museum is as interesting as the pyramids themselves
- 🚗 Difficult by public transport — best by car, 40 minutes from Santa Cruz on the TF-1
- 📸 The best photograph is from the elevated area of the park with Teide in the background
- 🌵 The park's botanical garden includes endemic Canarian species

### Recommendation
Ideal combined with a stop in the village of Güímar and the southeast viewpoints — a much less visited area with spectacular sea views.

pois.name: García Sanabria Park
pois.shortDescription: Santa Cruz's largest garden: urban art, fountains and century-old dragon trees
pois.description:
García Sanabria Park is the largest municipal garden in the Canary Islands and one of the archipelago's most beautiful green spaces. Opened in 1926, it covers six hectares in the centre of Santa Cruz and combines tropical gardens with a permanent collection of **contemporary outdoor sculpture**, the result of the 1973 International Sculpture Symposium.

### The visit
Royal palms, century-old ficus trees, monumental fountains and pieces by international sculptors coexist in a space that is simultaneously an urban park and an open-air museum. The **ancient dragon trees** — the symbolic tree of the Canary Islands — are the most impressive in Santa Cruz. The park is two minutes' walk from the Calatrava Auditorium and the Natural History and Archaeology Museum, making it the cultural hub of the city centre.

### Before you go
- 🆓 Free admission — open every day
- 🌿 Best visited in the morning, when light filters through the trees and the heat is still gentle
- 🖼️ The sculpture map is available at the entrance — there are more than 40 pieces throughout the park
- 📍 5 minutes' walk from the Calatrava Auditorium, the Nuestra Señora de África Market and Las Teresitas beach (by bus)
- 🍦 The ice cream stalls and terrace cafés on the adjacent avenue are a classic Santa Cruz afternoon

### Recommendation
Start the day in the park, continue to the Auditorium and end with a walk through the Africa market: the perfect route to discover the cultural heart of Santa Cruz.

pois.name: Masca
pois.shortDescription: Tenerife's most dramatic village: vertical ravines, cliff-hanging houses and silence
pois.description:
Masca is one of those places that leaves you speechless. Nestled in the Teno massif — the geologically oldest corner of Tenerife — the village clings to a ridge between sheer ravines at more than 700 metres altitude. When you arrive and look out at that landscape, you understand why this hamlet of fewer than 100 inhabitants appears on every list of Spain's most beautiful villages.

### The visit
The village itself is small: a handful of black volcanic stone houses with red-tiled roofs, terraces overlooking the abyss, a couple of restaurants serving papas and Teno cheese, and craft shops. The real attraction is the **surrounding landscape**: the Masca Ravine — descending to the sea through a canyon with 300-metre walls — is one of the most famous hiking routes in the Canary Islands. You can also visit Masca as a stop on a circular route through the north that takes in Los Gigantes, the Mirador de Cherfe and the Buenavista coast.

### Before you go
- 🚗 The TF-436 road is very narrow with tight bends — drive slowly, especially in campervans
- 🕐 Arrive before 10am to avoid tourist coaches and have the village almost to yourself
- 🏔️ If you hike the ravine, arrange your return: you can only come back by boat to Los Gigantes (book online) or climb back on foot
- 📸 The best viewpoint is 500m before reaching the village, by the roadside
- 🌡️ Temperature in the ravine rises sharply in summer — not recommended July to September

### Recommendation
Visit Masca early in the morning, have breakfast on a terrace overlooking the ravine and continue to Los Gigantes along the coast: one of the most spectacular days you can spend in Tenerife.

pois.name: Anaga Rural Park
pois.shortDescription: Europe's oldest laurel forest, in the far north of Tenerife
pois.description:
The Anaga Rural Park is one of Europe's most extraordinary natural treasures and yet one of the corners of Tenerife most overlooked by mass tourism. This mountain massif at the island's north-eastern tip is home to the **world's largest laurisilva forest** — a Tertiary-era relict ecosystem that survived the last ice age here in the Canary Islands.

### The visit
The laurisilva is a humid subtropical forest of breathtaking beauty: trees draped in moss and lichen, giant ferns, mist filtering through the canopy and an absolute silence broken only by the calls of endemic birds. The viewpoints of **Pico del Inglés** and **Cruz del Carmen** offer views over a sea of clouds covering the north of the island. From the villages of Taganana and El Bailadero you can access some of the island's best hiking routes.

### Before you go
- 🌫️ Mist is frequent — bring a warm layer even in summer
- 🚗 TF-12 road from La Laguna towards Pico del Inglés — winding but paved
- 🎒 The Cruz del Carmen Visitor Centre has trail maps and an ecosystem exhibition
- 🐦 The endemic Tenerife Robin is very easy to spot on the trails
- 🏖️ Combine with Playa de Benijo, 20 minutes away via the TF-134 from Taganana

### Recommendation
Head up early to Cruz del Carmen, walk 30 minutes through the laurisilva trail, stop at the Pico del Inglés viewpoint and descend to Taganana for lunch at one of its bars: a day of pure nature.

pois.name: Paisaje Lunar
pois.shortDescription: White volcanic pumice formations that simulate the surface of the Moon at 2,000m altitude
pois.description:
At 2,000 metres altitude, hidden within the Vilaflor pine forests, lies one of the most surreal landscapes in the Canary Islands: the **Paisaje Lunar**. Columns, needles and cones of **white and yellow volcanic tuff** eroded over millennia by water and wind create a setting that genuinely resembles the surface of the Moon.

### The visit
It is only accessible on foot, via the PR-TF 72 trail from the Vilaflor parking area (about 45 minutes of gentle uphill walking through Canarian pine forest). The formations stand between 2 and 5 metres tall and you can walk freely among them. The combination of white tuff against the deep blue sky at altitude creates spectacular photographic contrasts. On clear days, Teide looms impressively in the background.

### Before you go
- 🚗 Access via the TF-21 from Vilaflor — park in the designated area by the road (free)
- 🥾 Hiking boots recommended — the path has some gradient but is accessible
- ⏱️ The round trip takes 2–3 hours — better done in the morning
- 🌡️ Temperature at 2,000m is 8–10°C colder than the coast — bring a jacket
- 📸 Mid-morning light (10–12h) is best for photographing the white formations

### Recommendation
Combine Paisaje Lunar with a visit to Vilaflor village — Spain's highest village — and a stop at the Teide Cañadas: the most spectacular inland route on Tenerife.

pois.name: Mirador del Pico del Inglés
pois.shortDescription: Anaga's best viewpoint: 360° views over northern Tenerife and La Gomera
pois.description:
The Mirador del Pico del Inglés, at 992 metres altitude in the heart of the Anaga Rural Park, offers one of the most spectacular views in all of Tenerife and, on clear days, one of the most impressive island panoramas in the Atlantic. Its name comes from the old British tourists who climbed here in the 19th century to take in the landscape.

### The visit
From the viewpoint you can take in the entire Anaga massif: deep ravines carpeted in laurisilva, the Atlantic on the horizon, the silhouette of Gran Canaria to the south and La Gomera to the west. Below you, when clouds form, a **spectacular sea of clouds** covers the north of the island with Teide seemingly floating above it in the distance. The viewpoint is well equipped with railings and information panels.

### Before you go
- 🌫️ The viewpoint is frequently in cloud — check the Anaga webcam before heading up
- 🕐 Best visibility is usually early morning before the mist rises
- 🚗 TF-12 road from La Laguna, well signposted — free parking next to the viewpoint
- 📸 If there is a sea of clouds, the photo from here is among the most spectacular in Tenerife
- 🌿 The Cruz del Carmen laurisilva trail starts next to the viewpoint

### Recommendation
Get up early, arrive before 9am while the mist has not yet risen, and if you are lucky with the sea of clouds you will witness one of the most beautiful natural spectacles in the Canary Islands.

pois.name: Las Cañadas del Teide
pois.shortDescription: Spain's largest volcanic caldera: a sea of solidified lava at 2,000 metres
pois.description:
Las Cañadas del Teide are the heart of the National Park and the most lunar landscape in all of Spain. This **volcanic caldera 16 km in diameter** — the largest in the country — was formed by the collapse of an ancient supervolcano and is surrounded by walls up to 600 metres high. Inside, Teide and Pico Viejo dominate a landscape of solidified lavas in impossible colours.

### The visit
The Cañadas circular road (TF-21) is one of Europe's most spectacular drives: badlands of black lava, the Roques de García — volcanic formations 100 metres tall that resemble abstract sculptures — the Llano de Ucanca with its white volcanic sand surface, and the limitless horizons of a landscape that changes colour with the light throughout the day. The Parador Nacional de Las Cañadas sits inside the caldera and is the perfect base for those wanting to watch the sunrise from Teide.

### Before you go
- 🎫 The National Park is free — the cable car and summit access require online booking months in advance
- 🌡️ Temperature can drop to 0°C even in summer — always bring warm clothing
- 🔭 Light pollution is minimal — Las Cañadas is one of Europe's best astrotourism spots
- 🚗 TF-21 from La Orotava (north) or from Vilaflor (south) — the northern route has better views
- ⛽ No petrol stations in the Park — fill up before heading up

### Recommendation
Head up early, stop at the Roques de García for a 30-minute walk, take the cable car if you have a booking, and stay for sunset to watch Teide cast its triangular shadow over the northern clouds.

pois.name: Barranco del Infierno
pois.shortDescription: Tenerife's most famous hike: 80m waterfall and 200m canyon walls
pois.description:
The Barranco del Infierno is the most popular hiking trail on Tenerife and one of the most spectacular in the Canary Islands. It starts from the historic centre of Adeje and climbs through a canyon of vertical walls to a **permanent 80-metre waterfall** — the highest on Tenerife — all within a setting of lush subtropical vegetation entirely at odds with the beach tourism of the nearby south coast.

### The visit
The route is linear — 7.5 km there and back with around 350 metres of cumulative elevation gain. The trail follows the ravine floor, with narrow passages, wooden bridges over the water and sections where the walls close to just a few metres apart. The humid microclimate sustains a lush cover of ferns, tabaibas and tarajales. The waterfall at the end is the great reward.

### Before you go
- 🎟️ Advance booking is mandatory and daily numbers are limited — book on the Cabildo website
- 🥾 Hiking footwear is essential — terrain is uneven and parts are wet
- ⏱️ Duration: 3–4 hours return at a comfortable pace
- 🚗 Park in Adeje village — access to the ravine is on foot from the historic centre
- 💧 Carry at least 1.5 litres of water per person — it can be very hot in summer

### Recommendation
Start early (opening at 8am) to avoid the heat and the crowds. Book several days in advance, especially in peak season.

pois.name: Masca Ravine
pois.shortDescription: Tenerife's most epic descent: 5km through a 300m canyon to the sea
pois.description:
The Masca Ravine is the most epic hiking route on Tenerife and one of the most spectacular in all of Spain. The trail descends from the village of Masca through a **canyon with walls up to 300 metres tall**, ending at a secluded cove accessible only on foot or by boat. A 5 km journey that concentrates all the geological drama of the Teno massif.

### The visit
The descent takes between 2.5 and 3.5 hours over uneven terrain, with sections of scrambling, passages along the wet ravine floor and areas of subtropical vegetation contrasting with bare volcanic rock walls. At the end, a small **black-pebble beach** awaits beside the Atlantic. The return is obligatorily by **boat to Los Gigantes** — the cove has no other land access — and that boat crossing is itself part of the experience.

### Before you go
- 🎟️ Book your return boat BEFORE you start (departures from the cove at approx. 1pm, 3pm, 4pm) — without a booking you could get stranded
- 🥾 Hiking shoes with a rubber grip sole — there are wet and slippery sections
- ⏱️ Leave Masca early (8–9am) to reach the cove before the midday heat
- 💧 Minimum 2 litres of water per person — no water sources on the route
- ⚠️ Route is closed on rainy days or when there is flash flood risk

### Recommendation
Book the boat days in advance, arrive in Masca before 9am and sort the logistics before you set off: the reward at the end — a secluded cove and a boat ride past Los Gigantes cliffs — is worth every effort.

track.tips: Descent only. Return by boat from the cove to Los Gigantes — book in advance.

pois.name: Paisaje Lunar Trail (PR-TF 72)
pois.shortDescription: The path to the white volcanic tuff columns through pine forest at 2,000m altitude
pois.description:
The PR-TF 72 trail is the official route to Paisaje Lunar, one of Tenerife's most singular geological formations. The path runs entirely through the **Canarian pine forest of Vilaflor** — the highest on Tenerife — with the scent of resin and light filtering through the canopy until suddenly the pines open and the white tuff needles appear.

### The visit
The 6 km return trail has a gentle gradient of around 200 metres, following a well-marked forestry track. The Canarian pine forest at this altitude is impressive in its own right: trees 20–30 metres tall, the ground carpeted in pine needles and absolute silence broken only by the wind. Halfway along, views southward across the island — with the Atlantic on the horizon — are exceptional.

### Before you go
- 🚗 Park in the designated area next to the TF-21, approximately at km 64 (signposted)
- 🥾 Comfortable footwear — the trail is well maintained and requires no technical equipment
- 🌡️ In winter there can be snow or ice on the track — check conditions before setting out
- ⏱️ Total duration: 2.5–3.5h including a stop for photos at Paisaje Lunar
- 📸 The best light for photographing the formations is between 10am and 1pm

### Recommendation
Combine this trail with a visit to Teide National Park on the same day: both are on the TF-21 and together they make the best inland day out on Tenerife.

pois.name: Montaña Blanca — Teide Summit
pois.shortDescription: The hiking route to Teide's crater: 8km at 3,718m over solidified lava
pois.description:
The route from Montaña Blanca to Teide's crater is the most important mountain ascent on foot in Spain and one of the most spectacular in Europe. No cable car, no queues: just you, a trail of solidified lava and the Atlantic horizon far below. An experience very few people ever forget.

### The visit
The trail (TF-38) starts from the Montaña Blanca car park at 2,350 metres altitude and climbs 8 km to the Altavista Refuge (3,260m) and then to the crater (3,718m). The landscape changes dramatically with altitude: first red cinder lava, then Teide's eggs (egg-shaped lava formations), then bare volcanic rock and finally the crater rim with sulphur fumaroles. The summit requires a **free permit** from the National Park.

### Before you go
- 🎫 The crater permit is free but limited (200 people/day) — book at reservasparquesnacionales.es months in advance
- 🌄 Go up the afternoon before and sleep at the Altavista Refuge to reach the summit at dawn
- 🌡️ Summit temperature can reach -10°C even in summer — proper mountain gear is essential
- 💧 Drink water constantly — altitude dehydrates faster than you expect
- ⛑️ Altitude sickness can set in above 2,500m — rest if you feel dizzy or develop a headache

### Recommendation
Sleep at the Altavista Refuge, summit at dawn with the island buried in clouds below your feet, then descend by cable car: the finest mountain experience you can have in the Canary Islands.

track.tips: Free permit mandatory for the crater. Altavista Refuge available for overnight stay.

pois.name: Canarian Cuisine in Tenerife
pois.shortDescription: Papas arrugadas, mojo, gofio and the Atlantic's finest wines: the island's food guide
pois.description:
Canarian cooking in Tenerife is one of Spain's most original cuisines: a blend of Atlantic, American, African and Mediterranean influences with indigenous ingredients you will not find anywhere else. Away from the tourist strip, the island's gastronomy is a world of authentic flavours.

### The visit
**Papas arrugadas with mojo** are the most recognisable dish: small potatoes boiled in heavily salted water until a salt crust forms on the skin, served with green mojo (coriander and garlic) or red mojo (paprika and vinegar). **Gofio** — flour made from toasted grains, a legacy of the Guanche people — appears in soups, desserts and as a side dish. **Rancho canario**, **caldo de papas** and **potaje de berros** are the most traditional hearty stews. Wines from the Valle de La Orotava and the Tacoronte-Acentejo D.O. are among the finest Atlantic wines in the world.

### Before you go
- 🍽️ Best traditional food: Nuestra Señora de África market (Santa Cruz), Taganana (Anaga), San Andrés and northern villages like La Orotava
- 🌶️ Red mojo and green mojo are different enough that ordering both is compulsory
- 🍷 Look for wines with D.O. Tacoronte-Acentejo or Valle de La Orotava — listán negro and listán blanco are unique to Tenerife
- 🐟 Fresh fish (parrotfish, grouper, sea bream) grilled with mojo is the finest coastal meal
- 🍮 Bienmesabe and frangollo are the traditional desserts not to be missed

### Recommendation
Avoid the resort seafront restaurants and seek out the guachinches of the north: small family bars serving house wine and local tapas. This is the most authentic gastronomic experience on Tenerife.

pois.name: Playa de Radazul
pois.shortDescription: Dark sand, crystal-clear water and a relaxed atmosphere beside the marina
pois.description:
Hidden on the southeast coast of Tenerife, **Playa de Radazul** is one of the island's most pleasant and tranquil urban beaches. Protected by breakwaters that reduce the swell, it offers crystal-clear water and excellent bathing conditions virtually year-round. Its setting beside a marina adds a different feel to other Tenerife beaches, with views of sailing boats and leisure craft.

### The visit
The beach combines dark volcanic sand and small pebbles, stretching approximately 200 metres. Thanks to the artificial protection of the bay, the sea usually stays calm, making it a popular choice for families, swimmers and snorkelling enthusiasts. The seafront promenade leads to several restaurants, cafés and terraces with ocean views.

Steps away is the **Radazul Marina**, one of Tenerife's main recreational harbours, from which water sports and diving excursions depart. The water clarity makes this one of the best spots near Santa Cruz for observing marine life.

### Before you go
- 🏖️ Beach protected by breakwaters — calm water for most of the year
- 🤿 Excellent for snorkelling and diving thanks to water clarity
- 🚗 Parking relatively easy outside summer peak hours
- ☀️ South-facing — enjoys many hours of sun even in winter
- 🍽️ Restaurants and cafés along the promenade and marina
- 🚌 Public transport connections from Santa Cruz and La Laguna

### Recommendation
If you want a comfortable beach near Santa Cruz but away from the crowds of Las Teresitas, Radazul is one of the best alternatives. Combine a relaxed swim with a stroll around the marina and lunch facing the sea for a complete coastal day.

pois.name: Playa El Bollullo
pois.shortDescription: Spectacular wild beach of black sand beneath the La Orotava cliffs
pois.description:
Considered by many to be one of the most beautiful beaches on Tenerife, **Playa El Bollullo** is a wild strip of black volcanic sand at the foot of the dramatic cliffs of the Valle de La Orotava. Far from the major tourist resorts, it retains a natural character that recalls what the island's coastline looked like before the age of tourism.

### The visit
The beach stretches about 400 metres, surrounded by steep volcanic walls covered in vegetation. The contrast between the black sand, the deep blue of the Atlantic and the green banana plantations above creates one of the most photogenic coastal landscapes on Tenerife.

Access requires a short walk down from the car park or via paths through the banana groves. The surroundings are spectacular, although the sea can carry swell and currents, especially in winter and on rough days. It is therefore better suited to sunbathing and enjoying the scenery than to long-distance swimming.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Check sea conditions — currents can be strong on some days
- 🚶 Access via a stepped path from the car park area
- 📸 One of the most photogenic spots in northern Tenerife
- ☀️ Best visited in the morning or at sunset to avoid the hottest hours
- 🍌 The path passes through traditional banana plantations of the Valle de La Orotava
- 🍽️ Seasonal beach bar and nearby restaurant

### Recommendation
Combine the visit with a tour of the Valle de La Orotava or the nearby beaches of Los Patos and Ancón. El Bollullo offers one of the most authentic and wild coastal experiences on Tenerife, perfect for those seeking nature and spectacular scenery away from the crowds.

pois.name: Playa del Muelle
pois.shortDescription: Small historic cove beside the old fishing harbour of Puerto de la Cruz
pois.description:
Tucked into the heart of Puerto de la Cruz, **Playa del Muelle** is a tiny urban cove steeped in history. For centuries it was one of the main centres of maritime activity on the north coast of Tenerife, and it still preserves the charm of the old fishing harbour that gave the town its origins.

### The visit
This small beach of volcanic sand and pebbles is sheltered by the historic quay, creating a relatively calm bathing area when sea conditions allow. Its location is unbeatable: surrounded by traditional restaurants, terraces and some of the most iconic corners of Puerto de la Cruz.

From here there are magnificent views of the northern Tenerife coastline, with the profile of the Valle de La Orotava and Teide dominating the horizon on clear days. Steps away are Plaza del Charco, the seafront promenade and the historic fishing quarter of La Ranilla, one of the most characterful parts of town.

### Before you go
- 🏛️ One of the most historically significant beaches on Tenerife
- 🌊 Bathing conditions depend on swell and tides
- 📸 Excellent for photographs of the old town and harbour
- 🍽️ Surrounded by fresh fish and seafood restaurants
- 🚶 Perfect combined with a walk through Puerto de la Cruz
- ☀️ Local atmosphere year-round

### Recommendation
More than a full-day beach, Playa del Muelle is an essential stop for discovering the maritime history of Puerto de la Cruz. Pair it with a visit to Plaza del Charco, the La Ranilla quarter and the nearby Lago Martiánez to enjoy one of the most authentic areas of northern Tenerife.

pois.name: Playa del Castillo
pois.shortDescription: Wide black-sand beach beside the historic Castillo de San Felipe
pois.description:
Located at the western end of Puerto de la Cruz, **Playa del Castillo** is a long stretch of black volcanic sand combining historic heritage, Atlantic scenery and a much quieter atmosphere than the town's busier bathing areas. It takes its name from the nearby **Castillo de San Felipe**, a 17th-century fortress built to defend the north Tenerife coast from pirate raids.

### The visit
The beach forms part of the same coastal strip as Playa Jardín and shares its impressive views of the ocean and Teide. Its wide expanse of black sand gives a sense of space unusual for an urban beach.

The seafront promenade connects easily with the centre of Puerto de la Cruz and offers pleasant walks by the sea. The presence of the castle adds cultural interest, making the visit a perfect combination of history, landscape and coast.

Sea conditions can vary according to the Atlantic's mood, so always pay attention to flags and lifeguard warnings when the service is in operation.

### Before you go
- 🏰 Visit Castillo de San Felipe, one of the most important historic monuments in Puerto de la Cruz
- 🌊 Check sea conditions before swimming, especially in winter
- 📸 Magnificent views of Teide on clear days
- 🚶 Connected to Playa Jardín and the town's seafront promenade
- 🌅 Excellent spot to watch the sunset over the north coast
- 🍽️ Restaurants and cafés a short walk away

### Recommendation
Combine the visit with a walk to Playa Jardín and the Castillo de San Felipe. This is one of the best areas to understand the historic relationship between Puerto de la Cruz and the sea, while enjoying one of the widest urban beaches in northern Tenerife.

pois.name: Playa María Jiménez
pois.shortDescription: Small black-sand beach with a local feel on the Puerto de la Cruz coast
pois.description:
Away from the busier parts of the municipality, **Playa María Jiménez** is a small black volcanic sand beach frequented mainly by local residents. Its quiet, un-touristy character makes it an interesting choice for those wanting to discover a more authentic side of the north Tenerife coast.

### The visit
The beach sits beside the Punta Brava neighbourhood, in an area where the Atlantic shows its full force. Surrounded by volcanic formations and with open views over the north coast, it offers a different experience to the island's larger urban beaches.

Because of its exposure to the open sea, bathing conditions can vary considerably depending on the swell. On calm days you can enjoy the beach and the coastal setting; during heavy swell episodes, extra caution is needed.

Its main attraction is tranquillity. You will find no major tourist infrastructure here, just a simple coastal corner where you can watch daily life in Puerto de la Cruz and enjoy the Atlantic landscape.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Always check sea conditions before swimming
- 🏖️ Beach used mainly by local residents
- 📸 Good views of the north coast and Atlantic
- 🚶 Easy access from the urban area of Puerto de la Cruz
- ☀️ Quiet atmosphere for most of the year
- 🌋 Characteristic volcanic coast setting

### Recommendation
If you have already visited Playa Jardín and the better-known spots of Puerto de la Cruz, Playa María Jiménez offers a more authentic and less touristy view of the north coast. Easy to combine with a visit to the Punta Brava neighbourhood and the nearby Loro Parque.

pois.name: Playa San Telmo
pois.shortDescription: Historic central black-sand beach beside the Puerto de la Cruz seafront
pois.description:
In the heart of Puerto de la Cruz, **Playa San Telmo** is one of the most iconic bathing spots in northern Tenerife. Wrapped by the lively seafront promenade and the historic buildings of the town centre, it combines the traditional charm of the city with magnificent views over the Atlantic Ocean and the Valle de La Orotava.

### The visit
The beach is partly sheltered by volcanic formations and coastal walls that create a more protected bathing area than other parts of the north coast. Its black volcanic sand and privileged position make it one of the most accessible urban beaches on Tenerife.

Metres away are some of Puerto de la Cruz's best-known landmarks — the Paseo de San Telmo, Plaza del Charco and the Lago Martiánez complex. This location makes it a regular stop for both residents and visitors who want to combine beach, gastronomy and an urban stroll in a single day.

Sunsets from San Telmo are particularly popular, with open views towards the cliffs of the north coast and the Atlantic Ocean.

### Before you go
- 🏖️ One of the most centrally located urban beaches on Tenerife
- 🚶 Perfect combined with a visit to the historic town centre
- 🌊 Check sea conditions, especially during heavy swell
- 📸 Excellent views of the north coastline and Atlantic
- 🍽️ Surrounded by cafés, restaurants and terraces
- 🌅 Highly recommended at sunset

### Recommendation
Combine the beach with a walk along the Paseo de San Telmo, a visit to Lago Martiánez and dinner by the sea. One of the best areas to enjoy the historic and maritime atmosphere of Puerto de la Cruz without straying from the town centre.

pois.name: Playa de Los Abriguitos
pois.shortDescription: Small black-sand cove with a local feel beside the cliffs of southern Tenerife
pois.description:
Hidden along the Arico coast, **Playa de Los Abriguitos** is a small black volcanic sand cove that preserves the quiet, low-key character of traditional southern Tenerife. Far from the major tourist areas, it offers an authentic experience where the volcanic landscape and the Atlantic Ocean are the true protagonists.

### The visit
The beach is partly sheltered by rocky formations that help reduce the swell under certain conditions. Its small size and relaxed atmosphere attract mainly local residents and travellers seeking the island's lesser-known corners.

The setting is characterised by dark volcanic rock and open Atlantic views. The absence of large tourist infrastructure gives a sense of tranquillity that is increasingly hard to find elsewhere on the Tenerife coast.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Check sea conditions before swimming
- 🏖️ Small beach with a quiet, uncrowded atmosphere
- ☀️ Excellent climate for most of the year
- 📸 Good spot for photographing the volcanic south Tenerife coast
- 🚗 Recommended to arrive by car
- 🥤 Limited facilities on the beach itself

### Recommendation
Combine the visit with other coastal corners of the Arico municipality, such as Porís de Abona or the natural pools in the area. An ideal stop for those wanting to discover a less known, more authentic Tenerife.

pois.name: Playa de La Pinta
pois.shortDescription: Family-friendly golden-sand beach beside Puerto Colón marina
pois.description:
Located between Costa Adeje and Puerto Colón, **Playa de La Pinta** is one of the most popular family beaches in southern Tenerife. Its golden sand, calm water and position beside the island's main tourist marina make it ideal for those looking for comfort, services and water activities all in one place.

### The visit
The beach is protected by breakwaters that reduce swell and create a wide safe bathing area for families with children. Water usually remains calm year-round, perfect for swimming, paddleboarding and light water activities.

On one side sits **Puerto Colón**, the departure point for cetacean watching tours, boat trips, sport fishing and water sports. The seafront promenade connects easily with the nearby beaches of Torviscas and Fañabé, forming one of the liveliest stretches of the Costa Adeje coast.

### Before you go
- 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 One of the best family beaches in southern Tenerife
- 🌊 Usually calm water thanks to the protective breakwaters
- ⛵ Beside Puerto Colón, the main tourist marina in Costa Adeje
- ☀️ Excellent climate year-round
- 🍽️ Wide choice of restaurants, cafés and shops along the promenade
- 🚿 Sun loungers, parasols, showers and adapted accessibility

### Recommendation
Combine a few hours on the beach with a dolphin and whale watching excursion from Puerto Colón. La Pinta is one of the best options for a comfortable family day without straying from the wide leisure offering of Costa Adeje.

pois.name: Playa del Camisón
pois.shortDescription: Small golden-sand beach with calm water between Los Cristianos and Las Américas
pois.description:
Sitting between Playa de Las Américas and Los Cristianos, **Playa del Camisón** is one of the most well-kept and pleasant beaches in southern Tenerife. Its modest size, water quality and the landscaped surroundings make it a favourite for those seeking tranquillity without leaving the main tourist areas.

### The visit
The beach is protected by stone groynes that create a sheltered bay with calm water for most of the year. The golden sand — imported like many tourist beaches in the south — offers a comfortable experience for sunbathing and swimming.

One of its most distinctive features are the palms and gardens that border the beach, giving it a more elegant and relaxed atmosphere than other nearby coastal areas. It also forms part of the long promenade connecting Costa Adeje, Playa de Las Américas and Los Cristianos, allowing you to walk several kilometres along the sea.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Calm water thanks to the protective groynes
- 🌴 Landscaped, well-maintained surroundings
- 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Ideal for families and swimmers seeking calm conditions
- 🚶 Located beside the promenade between Los Cristianos and Las Américas
- ☀️ Excellent orientation and climate year-round
- 🍽️ Wide choice of restaurants, cafés and hotels nearby

### Recommendation
Combine the visit with a walk along the Golden Mile of Playa de Las Américas or a coastal stroll to Los Cristianos. Playa del Camisón offers one of the most pleasant and relaxed beach experiences in southern Tenerife.

pois.name: Playa de Torviscas
pois.shortDescription: Golden-sand beach with a lively atmosphere in the heart of Costa Adeje
pois.description:
Located between Puerto Colón and Playa Fañabé, **Playa de Torviscas** is one of the most popular beaches in Costa Adeje. Its wide strip of golden sand, calm water and extensive leisure and dining offering make it one of the busiest spots in southern Tenerife.

### The visit
The beach forms part of the long seafront promenade connecting Costa Adeje with Playa de Las Américas and Los Cristianos. Thanks to protective breakwaters, the swell is usually gentle for most of the year, creating ideal conditions for swimming and light water activities.

The atmosphere is lively and cosmopolitan, especially during the busiest tourist months. Along the promenade you will find terraces, restaurants, shops, ice cream parlours and numerous visitor-facing services.

From the beach there are magnificent views of La Gomera island, especially during clear sunsets. The closeness of Puerto Colón also provides easy access to boat excursions and sea activities.

### Before you go
- 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Ideal family beach thanks to calm water
- ☀️ Excellent climate year-round
- 🚶 Connected by promenade with Fañabé, La Pinta and Las Américas
- ⛵ Very close to Puerto Colón and its marine excursions
- 🍽️ Wide choice of restaurants, cafés and shops
- ♿ Accessible beach with extensive tourist services

### Recommendation
Combine the beach with a walk to Playa Fañabé or Puerto Colón. If you want a comfortable day with all services close by and a lively atmosphere, Torviscas is one of the best options in southern Tenerife.

pois.name: Playa de Troya
pois.shortDescription: The most iconic beach of Playa de Las Américas, with golden sand and a vibrant atmosphere
pois.description:
At the heart of Playa de Las Américas, **Playa de Troya** is one of the most famous and visited beaches in southern Tenerife. Its prime location, golden sand and the enormous leisure offering surrounding it have made it one of the main meeting points for visitors from around the world.

### The visit
The beach is divided into two sections — Troya I and Troya II — separated by a small promenade. Both areas have golden sand and are protected by breakwaters that reduce swell, providing calm water for much of the year.

Its location in the tourist centre means everything is within steps: restaurants, terraces, hotels, shops, shopping centres and one of the best-known nightlife areas on Tenerife. By day the atmosphere is family-friendly and relaxed; by late afternoon and evening the area takes on a livelier energy.

From the beach there are excellent views of La Gomera and Atlantic sunsets, especially in winter.

### Before you go
- ☀️ One of the sunniest beaches on Tenerife year-round
- 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Usually calm water thanks to the protective breakwaters
- 🚶 On the promenade connecting Costa Adeje, Las Américas and Los Cristianos
- 🍽️ Wide choice of restaurants, bars and shops nearby
- 🏄 Water sports available in nearby areas
- ♿ Accessible beach with extensive tourist services

### Recommendation
If you want beach, atmosphere, restaurants and the full tourist experience, Troya is one of Tenerife's best bets. Particularly enjoyable at sunset, when the promenade fills with visitors enjoying the views over the ocean.

pois.name: Playa de Las Vistas
pois.shortDescription: The great golden-sand beach between Los Cristianos and Playa de Las Américas
pois.description:
At nearly one kilometre long, **Playa de Las Vistas** is one of the most famous and visited beaches on Tenerife. Sitting between Los Cristianos and Playa de Las Américas, it stands out for its enormous stretch of golden sand, calm water and excellent accessibility, making it one of the finest urban beaches in the Canary Islands.

### The visit
The beach was artificially enlarged in the 1970s with golden sand and protected by breakwaters that reduce swell. As a result, it offers exceptional bathing conditions virtually year-round.

One of its most recognisable features is the fountain in the sea, visible from most of the beach. The wide promenade bordering it connects directly with Los Cristianos, Playa de Las Américas and Costa Adeje, allowing you to walk several kilometres along the ocean with virtually no interruption.

Las Vistas has every service you could want: sun lounger hire, showers, adapted access, water activities, restaurants, cafés and shopping areas. Its combination of comfort, size and location makes it one of the most complete beaches on Tenerife.

### Before you go
- 🏖️ One of the largest and most popular beaches on Tenerife
- 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Ideal for families thanks to calm water
- ♿ Fully accessible with adapted facilities
- 🚶 Connected by promenade with Los Cristianos, Las Américas and Costa Adeje
- ☀️ Excellent climate year-round
- 🍽️ Wide choice of restaurants, cafés and shops nearby

### Recommendation
If you are visiting southern Tenerife and can only pick one urban beach, Las Vistas is a safe bet. It combines swimming, a promenade, gastronomy and all the services you need for a complete day by the sea.

pois.name: Playa de Fañabé
pois.shortDescription: One of Costa Adeje's most popular beaches, with golden sand and full services
pois.description:
At the heart of Costa Adeje, **Playa de Fañabé** is one of the most famous and visited beaches in southern Tenerife. Its wide stretch of golden sand, calm water and extensive services have made it a favourite for families and visitors alike.

### The visit
The beach forms part of the great tourist seafront connecting Costa Adeje with Playa de Las Américas and Los Cristianos. Thanks to protective breakwaters, the water usually stays calm for most of the year, offering ideal conditions for swimming and light water activities.

The promenade is lined with restaurants, cafés, shops and hotels, creating a lively atmosphere throughout the day. Unlike more intensely urban beaches, Fañabé retains a sense of openness that allows you to find space even during the busiest periods.

Views of La Gomera and spectacular Atlantic sunsets are among its greatest attractions. The beach also has high-quality services including adapted access, sun lounger hire and water sports zones.

### Before you go
- 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 One of the best family beaches in southern Tenerife
- 🌊 Calm water thanks to the protective breakwaters
- ☀️ Excellent climate year-round
- 🚶 Connected by promenade with El Duque, Torviscas and La Pinta
- 🍽️ Wide choice of restaurants, cafés and shops
- ♿ Accessible beach with extensive facilities

### Recommendation
If you want a comfortable, wide beach with every service imaginable, Playa de Fañabé is a reliable choice. Combine it with a walk to Playa del Duque or Puerto Colón for one of the most complete tourist areas on Tenerife.

pois.name: Playa de La Tejita
pois.shortDescription: Tenerife's longest natural beach beside the iconic Montaña Roja
pois.description:
Over one kilometre long, **Playa de La Tejita** is one of the most spectacular and best-preserved natural beaches on Tenerife. Situated beside the Montaña Roja Natural Monument, it offers a unique landscape where dunes, golden sand and the reddish tones of the volcanic cone create one of the most emblematic images on the island.

### The visit
Unlike many tourist beaches in the south, La Tejita retains a wild, open-to-the-Atlantic character. Its vast expanse allows you to find space even during busier periods, while the absence of large developments near the beach contributes to a sense of nature that is increasingly rare elsewhere on the Tenerife coast.

The beach is divided into several areas, some more sheltered by the closeness of Montaña Roja and others more exposed to wind and swell. These conditions make it particularly popular with windsurfers, kitesurfers and other water sports enthusiasts.

The path circling Montaña Roja offers some of the best viewpoints in southern Tenerife, with panoramic views over La Tejita, El Médano and the Atlantic Ocean.

### Before you go
- 🏖️ One of the largest natural beaches on Tenerife
- 🌋 Located beside the Montaña Roja Natural Monument
- 💨 Frequently windy, especially in summer
- 🚶 Ideal combined with the climb up Montaña Roja
- 📸 One of the most photogenic coastal landscapes on the island
- ☀️ Great for enjoying sun and nature year-round

### Recommendation
Allow at least half a day to explore the area. Combine a beach walk with the climb up Montaña Roja for some of the best views in southern Tenerife. If you want nature, space and a less developed setting, La Tejita is unmissable.

pois.name: Playa Abama
pois.shortDescription: Exclusive golden-sand beach at the foot of the Guía de Isora cliffs
pois.description:
Hidden beneath the dramatic cliffs of Guía de Isora, **Playa Abama** is one of the most elegant and photogenic beaches on Tenerife. Its golden sand, crystal-clear water and spectacular natural setting make it one of the coastal gems of the west coast.

### The visit
The beach is protected by several groynes that keep the sea calm for much of the year, creating ideal conditions for swimming and snorkelling. Unlike other beaches in the south, Abama maintains a quieter, more exclusive atmosphere thanks to its secluded location and the luxury resort environment surrounding it.

Access is via a paved path descending from the clifftop above. Along the way there are spectacular views of the Atlantic and the island of La Gomera, especially at sunset.

The water quality and marine richness of the area make it one of the best spots on the west coast for snorkelling close to shore. The turquoise tones of the sea contrast with the volcanic cliffs and golden sand, creating one of the most impressive seascapes on the island.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Calm water thanks to the protective groynes
- 🤿 Excellent for snorkelling and observing marine life
- 🚶 Access via a paved path with a moderate gradient
- 📸 One of the most photogenic beaches on Tenerife
- 🌅 Magnificent views of La Gomera at sunset
- ☀️ Quieter atmosphere than Costa Adeje beaches

### Recommendation
Visit early morning or late afternoon for the best light and to avoid peak hours. Combine the beach with the viewpoints of Guía de Isora or the nearby Los Gigantes cliffs to discover one of the most spectacular areas on the west coast of Tenerife.

pois.name: Playa de Los Guíos
pois.shortDescription: The beach at the foot of the dramatic Los Gigantes cliffs
pois.description:
Few beaches in the Canary Islands can boast a setting as spectacular as **Playa de Los Guíos**. Located beside the Los Gigantes marina, this small black volcanic sand beach sits literally at the base of the colossal cliffs that give the village its name — rock walls rising over 600 metres above the Atlantic Ocean.

### The visit
The main protagonist here is not the beach but the landscape. The Los Gigantes cliffs form one of the most impressive natural monuments on Tenerife and give a sense of scale that is hard to find anywhere else on the island.

The beach has black volcanic sand and generally calm water thanks to the natural protection of the bay. From the shore you get some of the best photographs of the cliffs, especially in the early morning and at sunset.

Steps away is the Los Gigantes Marina, departure point for many cetacean watching tours, kayak routes and boat trips. This makes the beach an ideal stop during a day exploring the west coast of Tenerife.

### Before you go
- 🏔️ One of the most spectacular views on Tenerife
- 📸 Essential spot for photographing the Los Gigantes cliffs
- 🌊 Usually calm water, though always check sea conditions
- ⛵ Beside the marina and sea excursions
- 🌅 Excellent for watching the sunset over the Atlantic
- 🍽️ Restaurants, cafés and services a short walk away

### Recommendation
Combine the swim with a boat trip to see the Los Gigantes cliffs from the sea. The experience of seeing these enormous volcanic walls both from the beach and from the ocean is one of the most impressive memories a visitor can take away from Tenerife.

pois.name: Natural Pools of Bajamar
pois.shortDescription: Spectacular ocean pools beside the Atlantic on the north coast of Tenerife
pois.description:
The **Natural Pools of Bajamar** are one of the most iconic bathing complexes in northern Tenerife. Located beside the Atlantic Ocean in the municipality of San Cristóbal de La Laguna, they combine the power of the sea with conditioned pools that allow you to enjoy the water for most of the year.

### The visit
The complex consists of two large saltwater pools and several bathing areas adapted for different ages. On days of heavy swell, the spectacle of waves breaking against the outer walls makes the visit an unforgettable experience.

The pools offer magnificent views over the Atlantic and the rugged Anaga massif coastline. Their size and the quality of the facilities attract both locals and visitors seeking a safe alternative to the open beaches of the north.

The Bajamar seafront promenade allows you to explore the coast comfortably, with restaurants, cafés and viewpoints along the way. On clear days Teide can be seen rising above the island landscape.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Conditioned saltwater pools for swimming
- 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Perfect for families and visitors of all ages
- 📸 Spectacular during Atlantic storms and heavy swells
- 🚶 Seafront promenade with views over the Atlantic
- 🍽️ Restaurants and cafés nearby
- ☀️ Very pleasant during summer and autumn months

### Recommendation
Combine the visit with a tour of Bajamar, Punta del Hidalgo or the trails of the Anaga Rural Park. The natural pools are one of the best places on the north coast of Tenerife to enjoy the sea safely and comfortably while taking in some of the island's most impressive coastal scenery.

pois.name: Natural Pool of Punta del Hidalgo
pois.shortDescription: Ocean pools with spectacular views over the Anaga massif and the Atlantic
pois.description:
At the north-eastern tip of Tenerife, the **Natural Pools of Punta del Hidalgo** offer one of the island's most authentic coastal experiences. Built beside the Atlantic and surrounded by the spectacular landscape of the Anaga massif, they combine the force of the sea with safe and accessible bathing areas.

### The visit
The complex consists of several saltwater pools cut and conditioned along the coast, allowing you to enjoy the ocean even when the sea is rough. The location is privileged: facing the open Atlantic and the impressive cliffs marking the entrance to the Anaga Rural Park.

On days of heavy swell, waves breaking against the volcanic formations and outer walls create an extraordinary natural spectacle. On calm days, the pools become a perfect place to relax, swim and take in the landscape.

The seafront promenade connects the pools with the iconic Punta del Hidalgo Lighthouse and several restaurants specialising in fresh fish and traditional Canarian cooking.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Conditioned saltwater pools beside the ocean
- 🏔️ Spectacular views over the Anaga massif
- 📸 One of the most photogenic corners of northern Tenerife
- 🚶 Easy access from the Punta del Hidalgo seafront promenade
- 🌅 Magnificent Atlantic sunsets
- 🍽️ Restaurants and terraces a few minutes' walk away

### Recommendation
Combine the visit with a hike through the Anaga trails, a walk to the Punta del Hidalgo Lighthouse or lunch by the sea. One of the best places on Tenerife to enjoy the ocean safely while taking in some of the island's most spectacular scenery.

pois.name: Natural Pool of Mesa del Mar
pois.shortDescription: Ocean pool beside the Tacoronte cliffs with spectacular Atlantic views
pois.description:
Located in the small coastal village of Mesa del Mar in the municipality of Tacoronte, the **Natural Pool of Mesa del Mar** is one of the quietest and most authentic corners of northern Tenerife. Surrounded by impressive volcanic cliffs and open to the Atlantic Ocean, it offers a very different experience to the island's major tourist areas.

### The visit
The pool is conditioned along the coast and fed directly from the sea. Its protected design allows swimming in greater safety than many open stretches of the north coast.

The setting is dominated by spectacular cliff walls and panoramic Atlantic views. On days of heavy swell, the sea puts on an impressive show with waves crashing against nearby volcanic formations.

Very close is the Playa de Mesa del Mar, a small black-sand beach that complements the visit perfectly. The atmosphere is usually quiet and frequented mainly by local residents.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Saltwater pool protected from direct swell
- 🏔️ Spectacular views of the Tacoronte cliffs
- 📸 Excellent spot for coastal photography
- 🏖️ Beside the Playa de Mesa del Mar
- 🚗 Road access from Tacoronte
- ☀️ Quiet, uncrowded atmosphere for most of the year

### Recommendation
Combine the visit with a tour of the Tacoronte coast and viewpoints in the area. An ideal spot for those seeking a more local and relaxed experience away from the main tourist centres, while enjoying one of the most striking coastal landscapes in northern Tenerife.

pois.name: Charco de La Laja
pois.shortDescription: Spectacular volcanic natural pool among lava flows on the north Tenerife coast
pois.description:
**Charco de La Laja** is one of the most photogenic and surprising natural pools on Tenerife. Located in the municipality of San Juan de la Rambla, this volcanic corner was formed by ancient lava flows that created a natural pool sheltered from the Atlantic swell. The contrast between black rock, crystal-clear water and the open ocean makes this one of the most spectacular coastal landscapes on the north coast.

### The visit
The natural pool is set between volcanic formations that act as a natural barrier against the sea. When conditions are favourable, its transparent waters take on turquoise tones that contrast dramatically with the intense black of the lava.

One of its greatest attractions is the sensation of swimming in a natural pool sculpted by nature itself. On calm days it is an excellent place to swim and relax. However, when there is heavy swell or rough seas, conditions can become dangerous and extreme caution is needed.

Access is via steps from the San Juan de la Rambla seafront promenade, which also offers magnificent views over the north Tenerife coast.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Always check sea conditions before swimming
- 📸 One of the most photogenic natural pools on Tenerife
- 🌋 Formed by ancient volcanic lava flows
- 🚶 Access via steps from the coastal path
- ☀️ Best visited in favourable tide and weather conditions
- ⚠️ Avoid swimming during heavy swell or rough seas

### Recommendation
Visit in the morning for the best light on the crystal-clear water. Combine it with a tour of San Juan de la Rambla and other coastal corners of northern Tenerife. One of those places that perfectly illustrates the volcanic origins of the Canary Islands.

pois.name: El Caletón
pois.shortDescription: Tenerife's most famous natural pools, created by the 1706 volcanic eruption
pois.description:
Few places on Tenerife illustrate the power of nature better than **El Caletón**. Located beside the historic town centre of Garachico, this spectacular series of natural pools was born from the 1706 volcanic eruption, when lava flows completely transformed the town's original harbour. Today it is one of the most iconic and photographed spots on the island.

### The visit
The pools are distributed among volcanic formations that reached the sea more than three centuries ago, creating a set of rock pools and bathing areas of different sizes where the Atlantic constantly refreshes the water.

Conditioned walkways allow you to explore the complex easily and take in spectacular views of the north Tenerife coast. On calm days the pools offer excellent bathing conditions. When the Atlantic shows its full force, waves breaking against the rocks create one of the most impressive natural spectacles in the Canary Islands.

Metres away are some of Garachico's most important landmarks — the Castillo de San Miguel, the Plaza de la Libertad and the historic old harbour — making the visit a perfect combination of nature and history.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Check sea conditions before swimming
- 🌋 Formed by the 1706 lava flows
- 📸 One of the most photographed spots on Tenerife
- 🚶 Easy access from Garachico's historic centre
- 🏛️ Perfect combined with a cultural visit to the town
- ⚠️ Some areas may close for safety during storms

### Recommendation
Spend several hours exploring Garachico and finish the visit at El Caletón. Few experiences better reflect the volcanic history of the Canary Islands than bathing in natural pools created by an eruption that permanently changed the fate of one of Tenerife's most important historical towns.

pois.name: Charco Los Chochos
pois.shortDescription: Hidden natural pool among volcanic flows on the Los Silos coast
pois.description:
Located on the coast of Los Silos, **Charco Los Chochos** is one of the most attractive natural spots in the north-west of Tenerife. This natural pool, formed by ancient volcanic flows, offers a spectacular setting where the Atlantic Ocean and the island's volcanic geology combine to create a unique landscape.

### The visit
The pool is partly sheltered by lava formations that cushion the direct impact of waves, creating a wide saltwater bathing area. On calm days its waters take on blue-turquoise tones that contrast with the intense black of the volcanic rock.

The area has conditioned access and platforms that make entering the water easier. Its size makes it a very popular option among residents of northern Tenerife during the warmer months.

From the surroundings there are magnificent views of the Los Silos coast, the Teno massif and the cliffs that characterise this part of the island. The landscape is especially spectacular at sunset.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Always check sea conditions before swimming
- 🌋 Natural pool formed by ancient volcanic lava flows
- 📸 Excellent spot for volcanic coast photography
- 🚶 Relatively easy access from the urban area
- ☀️ Very popular with residents during summer
- ⚠️ Avoid swimming in heavy swell or rough seas

### Recommendation
Combine the visit with a tour of Los Silos, Buenavista del Norte or the nearby Teno Rural Park. Charco Los Chochos is an excellent alternative for those seeking an authentic natural pool away from Tenerife's busier spots.

pois.name: César Manrique Maritime Park
pois.shortDescription: Saltwater pool complex designed by César Manrique facing the Atlantic
pois.description:
The **César Manrique Maritime Park** is one of the most iconic leisure spaces in Santa Cruz de Tenerife. Designed by the celebrated Canarian artist and architect César Manrique and opened in 1995, it combines architecture, nature and the sea in a spectacular saltwater pool complex facing the Atlantic Ocean.

### The visit
The complex covers more than 22,000 square metres and features several saltwater pools, waterfalls, sunbathing terraces, palm gardens and rest areas integrated in a setting inspired by the volcanic aesthetics of the Canary Islands.

Manrique's philosophy is present in every corner, where volcanic stone, native vegetation and water create a perfect harmony between art and nature. Thanks to its position facing the sea, it offers magnificent views of the Atlantic and the Tenerife Auditorium.

In addition to the pools, the park has restaurants, cafés, children's areas and event spaces, making it one of the most popular places to enjoy Santa Cruz's excellent climate year-round.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Several saltwater pools of different depths
- 🎨 Designed by Canarian artist César Manrique
- 🌴 Wide landscaped areas and sunbathing terraces
- 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Ideal for families and visitors of all ages
- 🍽️ Restaurants, cafés and services within the complex
- 📸 Excellent views of the Tenerife Auditorium and the Atlantic

### Recommendation
Combine the visit with a walk to the Tenerife Auditorium, the Palmetum or the historic centre of Santa Cruz. One of the best options for enjoying the sea and sun in the island capital, especially if you want comfort and all services in one place.

pois.name: Lago Martiánez
pois.shortDescription: César Manrique's masterpiece in Puerto de la Cruz: saltwater lagoons and volcanic art
pois.description:
The **Costa Martiánez Tourist Complex**, popularly known as **Lago Martiánez**, is one of the most emblematic spaces on Tenerife and one of César Manrique's most important works. Opened in 1977 facing the Atlantic Ocean, this spectacular complex combines saltwater pools, gardens, sculptures and architecture integrated into the volcanic landscape of the Canary Islands.

### The visit
The complex covers more than 100,000 square metres and is formed by a large central artificial lagoon surrounded by several pools, islets, waterfalls and landscaped areas. The black volcanic stone, subtropical vegetation and sculptures designed by César Manrique create a unique environment where art and nature coexist in perfect harmony.

Located in the heart of Puerto de la Cruz, it offers impressive views of the Atlantic Ocean and the north Tenerife coast. In addition to the bathing areas, the complex has restaurants, terraces and spacious areas to relax in the sun.

The work is considered one of the finest examples of landscape architecture in the Canary Islands and one of the most recognised projects of César Manrique's artistic legacy outside Lanzarote.

### Before you go
- 🎨 Designed by César Manrique, one of the most influential figures in Canarian art
- 🌊 Multiple pools and a large saltwater lagoon
- 🌴 Wide landscaped areas and sunbathing spaces
- 📸 One of the most photogenic places in Puerto de la Cruz
- 🍽️ Restaurants and services within the complex
- 🚶 Just a few minutes from the historic centre of the town

### Recommendation
Dedicate at least half a day to enjoy the complex and combine it with a visit to the Paseo de San Telmo, Plaza del Charco or Playa Jardín. Lago Martiánez is much more than a bathing area: it is one of the most important open-air artworks in the Canary Islands and an unmissable visit in Puerto de la Cruz.

pois.name: Whale & Dolphin Watching on Eco Yacht
pois.shortDescription: The only yacht in Tenerife purpose-built for ethical whale and dolphin watching, with a swimming stop at the Cueva del Amor
pois.description:
